mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth decelerates below its 12-month moving average while the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rebounds above its 6-month moving average while the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy cycle, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% while the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending declines and corporate earnings prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: If UNRATE remains above 4.5% while the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a 3-month increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average, signals a strengthening consumer demand environment that typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: If either GDPC1 or HOUST growth decelerates below their 12-month moving averages while the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5%, combined with a 3-month decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below its 12-month moving average, signals a tightening monetary policy cycle with moderating inflation, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If either FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% or CPIAUCSL remains below its 12-month moving average while the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5%, combined with a 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below its 12-month moving average, signals a weakening labor market with declining consumer demand, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: If either UNRATE remains above 4.5% or GDPC1 remains below its 12-month moving average while the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, combined with a 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below its 12-month moving average, signals weakening manufacturing activity with declining consumer demand, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: If either INDPRO or GDPC1 rebounds above their respective moving averages while the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
